# Paint

> A local-first sketchpad PWA: draw a concept on a canvas, switch extra tools on
> when you need them, and keep every drawing on your device — with optional
> Dropbox or Google Drive sync.

Paint is a small, installable web app for sketching the kind of diagram you draw
to explain something: boxes, arrows, a circled bit, a scribble. Drawings are
vector strokes stored as JSON in your browser; nothing is uploaded unless you
connect a storage backend yourself.

## What it does

- Draw with a pencil, a bristle paintbrush, an eraser, a paint bucket, a colour
  dropper, a text tool, the shapes and a selection marquee, plus a hand tool that
  drags the page around — the toolbar out of the box.
- Draw eleven shapes from one toolbar button: rectangle, ellipse, line, arrow,
  rounded rectangle, triangle, diamond, pentagon, hexagon, star and double
  arrow. Press the button a second time for the family and the fill toggle.
- Pick marks up again with the selection tool: drag a box over what you drew,
  move it with the hand, and copy, cut or delete it with the keyboard, a
  right-click or a long press. Ctrl/Cmd+V pastes marks, a picture or words back
  into the drawing — words open the caption box so the typeface and size are
  yours to set first.
- Switch more tools on in Settings → Tools (airbrush, marker, highlighter,
  crayon, calligraphy pen), and drag the rows into the order you want the
  toolbar in. Every tool is a plugin behind one interface, so the list grows
  without the app changing shape.
- Type on the page: the text tool opens a caret where you tap, in four
  typefaces, five type sizes, bold and italic.
- Pick colour and stroke width from two buttons: a palette with a free colour
  mixer that remembers what you mix, and a nib picker with your own widths. The
  width is remembered per tool, and each tool opens at a width of its own.
- Tune the tool in your hand under the nib picker's Advanced fold — hair gauge
  for the paintbrush, flow for the airbrush, pressure for the crayon, a
  feathered edge for the paint bucket, opacity for most of the rest. Each tool
  keeps its own settings, and a mark remembers what it was drawn with.
- Start a drawing from an empty page, an image file, or an image on the
  clipboard. An empty one asks its canvas size up front — this screen, Full HD,
  4K or A4, drawn to one shared scale so the four can be compared at a glance.
- Draw on a page bigger than the window: the canvas is a window onto it, with
  pinch-to-zoom, two-finger panning, and one-finger panning under the hand.
- Stack a drawing into layers: swipe in from the right edge of the canvas (or
  use the header button) for a panel that adds, selects, shows, hides, reorders
  and deletes them, each row previewing the marks on that layer. New marks land
  on the selected layer; a hidden layer leaves the screen and every export.
- Keep several drawings, group them into folders, star the ones you return to,
  and archive the rest instead of deleting them.
- Tidy the sidebar with the gesture at hand: on touch, swipe a row right to
  archive it or left to bare a Delete button, and hold it to pick it up and drag
  it onto a folder, out to the top level, onto another sketchbook, or onto the
  archive — every target outlines itself as the row lifts. On a desktop the same
  actions live behind a right-click menu, and rows drag with the mouse.
- Keep several namespaces (separate sketchbooks), each with its own document,
  and move a drawing (or a whole folder, drawings and all) between them by
  dragging it onto another sketchbook's row.
- Drop an image file onto the canvas to add it to a drawing — move and scale it
  before settling it, and the page grows if the picture is bigger than the sheet
  — or onto the drawings list to start a new drawing named after the file.
- Undo and redo every mark; download a page as PNG, JPG or SVG, copy it to the
  clipboard, or export the whole document as JSON. Settings → Download chooses
  which types the menu offers, whether a file covers the whole page or crops to
  the marks, and whether the background is kept or transparent.
- Work offline: it is an installable PWA with a precaching service worker.
- Optionally sync to a local folder, Dropbox, or Google Drive, with optional
  end-to-end encryption of the synced file.
